dialog.body: Utilities, water and sewer billing, this is Tony. How can I help you?

Hi Tony, Sean Reardon, I'm at 92 Narragansett Avenue, and I got my water and sewer bill last week and it's way higher than normal, and the reason is a pipe broke in my basement back in December, the line coming off the meter, I had a plumber in to fix it, I've got the receipt for that, and on top of it the toilet was running constantly last month, I didn't notice for probably two weeks, so between the two I figure the usage is up, and I want to know if there's a leak adjustment, how that works, what I have to send you.

Okay, got it. Sure, there's a process for that. So a leak adjustment is basically a review where the city looks at your usage during the leak period compared to your usual usage. If the extra water was from a leak that's been repaired, they can sometimes adjust part of the charge. Mostly it's the water portion, and it depends on the details. Let me ask a couple of things. The broken pipe, was that before the meter or after the meter?
After. It's on my side, in the basement, between the meter and the water heater. Plumber replaced about six feet of copper. Date on the invoice is the twelfth of December.
Good, that's the homeowner side, so that's the kind of thing the adjustment is for. And the toilet, did you replace the flapper or have it repaired?
I replaced the flapper myself, the fill valve too, I kept the receipt from the hardware store, it was a few days into January when I did it.

Perfect. Hang on to both receipts. What you'll want to do is send a short written request, your name, the address, your account number from the bill, a description of what happened and the dates, and copies of the plumber invoice and the hardware store receipt. Don't send originals. You can drop it at the office or mail it.
Can I email it?
I'd say bring it by or mail it, that's the surest way to get it logged. If you want to double check on email, I can have somebody from the billing office confirm when they call you back.

No, I'll just drop it off. Next question, the bill itself is due, I think, this week, and I'm not sure I'm going to get down there during your hours. I'm going to the drugstore later this afternoon to get a passport photo taken, and then I'm home. If I put the payment in the drop box tonight, does that count as on time?

Yeah, there's a payment drop box outside City Hall, and it's available after hours. Generally, if it's in the box by the due date, it's treated as received that day. Just make sure the check has your account number on it and put it in an envelope. If you're paying close to the deadline, I'd say write the account number on the memo line so it can't get separated.
Okay. And should I pay the whole thing, or wait on the adjustment?

Good question. Usually you'd pay the bill by the due date so it doesn't go late, and if an adjustment comes through, it gets credited to your account afterward. Or if you pay the usual amount you normally pay, that's a way some folks do it. But I'd confirm that with the billing office when you drop off your request. They can tell you what to do for your account.
All right. How long does the review take?
A few weeks, typically. I don't want to tell you an exact number. They'll send you something in writing with the result.
Fine. Can you note my number in case they need to call? It's 401-555-0163.
Got it, 401-555-0163. I'll add a note that you're submitting a leak adjustment request for 92 Narragansett Avenue, pipe repair in December and a toilet issue in January.
That's right. Okay, that's everything. Thanks, Tony.
You're welcome, Mr. Reardon. Have a good afternoon, and good luck with the passport photo.
Thanks. Bye.
